cards.text: Paul writes this letter with Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Three names on one letter. That's a group chat where everybody actually REPLIES.

cards.question: Before anything else, Paul sends the Thessalonians a blessing from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. What does he wish them?

cards.text: Then Paul says he and his team are "obligated to thank God for you all the time." Obligated! Like it's a bill that's due, except this is the one bill a man is HAPPY to pay.

cards.question: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians because their faith keeps ___ more and more.
Paul says the Thessalonians' love for one another is starting to cool off.

cards.text: Paul doesn't keep it quiet, either. He boasts about them among God's churches, and friend, I get it, because if I had a phone you'd be scrolling through pictures of my kids RIGHT NOW.

cards.question: Paul boasts about the Thessalonians among God's churches. What does he boast about?
Paul says the Thessalonians keep up their perseverance and faith in the face of what?

answers.text: A long famine in the land

cards.text: Then Paul says something you might not see coming: "All this is clear evidence of God's righteous judgment." Stay with him, friend. He's going somewhere with this.

cards.question: Paul says the Thessalonians' suffering shows they are not worthy of the kingdom of God.

cards.text: Now Paul talks about what's fair. He says "it is only right for God to repay with affliction those who afflict you."

cards.question: God repays the ones afflicting the Thessalonians. What does Paul say it's right for God to give the Thessalonians who are oppressed?
Paul says this relief is for the Thessalonians only, not for Paul and his team.
Paul says all this will take place when the Lord Jesus is revealed from ___.

cards.text: And the Lord Jesus doesn't come quietly. He's revealed with His mighty angels in blazing fire, inflicting vengeance.

cards.question: When the Lord Jesus is revealed in blazing fire, who does Paul say He inflicts vengeance on?

answers.text: Those who do not know God or obey the gospel
Those who never kept the feasts in Jerusalem
Those who never made an offering at the temple

cards.text: Paul doesn't soften it. They will suffer the penalty of eternal destruction, separated from the presence of the Lord and the glory of His might.

cards.question: On the day Jesus comes, Paul says He will be regarded with wonder by all who have believed, and the Thessalonians are included.

cards.text: So what do Paul and his team do in the meantime? They pray for the Thessalonians ALWAYS, and friend, I've got timers all over this bakery and I STILL forget a batch.

cards.question: Paul prays that God will count the Thessalonians worthy of what?
What else does Paul pray that God will powerfully do for the Thessalonians?

answers.text: Fulfill every good desire and work of faith
Turn every one of their enemies into friends
Make them leaders over every nearby city

cards.question: Paul prays that the name of the Lord Jesus will be glorified in the Thessalonians, and they in ___.

cards.text: And it all comes "according to the grace of our God and of the Lord Jesus Christ." Grace at the start, grace at the end, like a cookie with chocolate chips on the top AND the bottom, and friend, that's the BEST kind.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "obligated to thank God for you all the time.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.
He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "it is only right for God to repay with affliction those who afflict you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.
A blank is a word that matters to the meaning, never a word like "or," "and" or "he."

findings.problem: Silvanus and Timothy show up for the first time, and nothing says who they are. They are only named as co-senders.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke's comparison doesn't share the core action. Three people sending one letter together is not a group chat where everyone replies. Co-signing is not replying, so the image doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the exact words of the letter's greeting ('Grace and peace'). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'holding' and 'resting' don't read naturally in 'faith keeps ___ more and more.' Only 'growing' fits the sentence, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The right answer changes the text's 'do not know God and do not obey the gospel' to 'do not know God or obey the gospel.' Swapping 'and' for 'or' widens the group the text describes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: 'In the meantime' adds a time link the text doesn't give. Verse 11 says 'To this end, we always pray for you,' which is a purpose link, not a meanwhile.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: No card tells that on that day the Lord comes 'to be glorified in His saints' (1:10). That is a key detail of the passage's climax, and the walkthrough skips it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
